senses.gloss:
yūpa
(‘sacrificial post’)
------------------------------------------
Among the वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्, about thirty are classed as पशु or Paśuyāgas, wherein an animal is immolated. The post to which this animal is tied is called यूप or yūpastambha.
It is to be made of wood. The trees out of which they are prepared are: palāśa (Butea frondosa); khadira (Acacia catechu); बिल्व (Aegle marmelos) and rauhitaka (Andersonia rohitaka).
Even for the selecting and the cutting of these trees, many rules have been prescribed. Along with the carpenter and the wood-cutter, the yajamāna (sacrificer) and the अध्वर्यु priest should also be present.
The standard unit of यूप’s measurement is aratni, one-fifth of the height of the yajamāna. The height of the यूप varies from 1 to 33 aratnis, depending on the type of the sacrifice. Usually it is 3 or 4 aratnis.
The lowest part called upara is one-fifth of the total height and is not chiselled. It is this part that is to be buried under ground.
The shape of the यूप is octagonal, with one face being wider than the other seven. This portion should face the sacrificial fire. Its height is that of the yajamāna in the standing posture, with or without the hands raised.
The girth of the यूप is not fixed. Its top has a cap called caṣāla, made of the wood leftover, after preparing the यूप proper.
